title: Canary VPC topology & safe-upgrade Terraform module for subnets, routes, and endpoints
creator: Aisha Malhotra
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module that performs safe topology upgrades for Private (VPC) deployments. The module will manage AZ-aware subnets, managed route tables, NAT gateway (or managed NAT replacement) lifecycle, IGW attachment, and VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, Secrets Manager) with automated pre-upgrade health probes and canary rollouts. Goal: allow Private installs to apply network topology changes with automated verification and automatic rollback on failures, minimizing customer downtime and manual intervention.
background: Customers running Redwood Private have expressed concern about applying network upgrades (subnet resize, route table adjustments, endpoint policy changes) without risking application breakage. Existing Terraform modules handle static provisioning but lack baked-in pre/post validations and staged rollouts. This ticket consolidates upgrade safety patterns into a single module used by on-prem and VPC templates.
acceptance_criteria: New terraform module 'redwood_vpc_safe_upgrade' implements canary_subnet pattern with per-az canary deployment toggles
Module exposes pre_upgrade_probe and post_upgrade_probe hooks that can be wired to a Lambda/StepFunction or external healthchecker
When enabled, module creates canary route tables and temporary NAT/IGW attachments for canary traffic without changing primary production routes
Apply plan includes a validation phase: terraform plan -> trigger synthetic probe -> on success proceed with staged apply -> on failure abort and provide remediation hints
Automated rollback path demonstrated in CI: create deliberate failure and verify module reverts to previous route table associations and removes canary resources
Comprehensive unit and integration tests in CI that run against a sandbox account: subnet changes, route propagation, VPC endpoint policy updates, and NAT failover scenarios
Documentation: README with usage examples for single-tenant and multi-tenant Private installs, migration steps, and operator runbook
Security review completed and IAM least-privilege templates provided for automation-runner role
implementation_notes: Module will use a modular subresource model: subnets, route_tables, endpoint_configs, nat_cluster
Prefer managed NAT replacement (elastic nat instances pooled with autoscaling) where customers have limits on NAT gateway quota
Use Terraform null_resource + local-exec to trigger synthetic probes or better: integrate AWS Lambda invoke via aws_lambda_invocation resource if available
Leverage tags and a 'canary=true' tag to segregate canary objects for easy cleanup
Add 'lifecycle' blocks to critical resources to avoid accidental destroys during plan/apply while canary = true
Provide outputs for route_table_attachments and endpoint_status to be consumed by operator tools and console
Design hook to integrate with Redwood Controller (internal orchestration) or run standalone via CI pipeline

open_questions: What's the recommended default probe timeout and retry policy for customers with strict SLOs?
Should we expose a pluggable probe implementation (HTTP/TCP/ICMP/agent) or keep a single Lambda-based synthetic checker?
How to surface staged progress in Console: should we create a new 'network-upgrade' rollout type or reuse existing rollout APIs?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Terraform-driven canary resources could accidentally persist if rollback fails. Mitigation: ensure automated cleanup run and 'canary_cleanup' flag default true, and provide operator alerting if cleanup did not complete.
Risk: IAM permissions too broad for probe runners. Mitigation: create scoped IAM templates and require security_review_required=true before enabling auto-upgrade in production tenants.
Risk: Probe false-positives lead to unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: make probe thresholds configurable and require 2 consecutive failed probe runs before aborting staged apply.
